public_rationale: On the ordinary reading of a categorical failure to win meaningful Wall Street confidence, the claim is contradicted. Yahoo Finance reported that Goldman Sachs viewed Alphabet as the premier AI innovator following I/O. Earlier Gemini problems and an adverse market reaction are real countercontext, but they do not erase that later institutional endorsement. This does not establish that all, or most, investors were convinced.
limitations: The result depends on reading failed as a categorical absence of meaningful acceptance, rather than failure to convince a specified majority.
Evidence of institutional opinion comes from reporting rather than an original research note.
No claim is made that AI alone caused Alphabet's stock performance.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google has failed to convince Wall Street that it is building and selling the AI future.

statement.excerpt: While Google has desperately tried (and failed) to convince Wall Street that it’s building and selling the future

from_speaker: that it’s building and selling the future
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that Google's AI pitch had failed to win meaningful confidence among Wall Street analysts and investors by the post date.
Assess expressed confidence in Google's AI competitive and commercial position. Do not require investors to endorse the literal phrase building and selling the future.
The claim retrospectively describes Google's efforts through publication and supplies no start date. Recent reactions carry more weight than earlier setbacks.
Share-price changes alone cannot establish what investors believed or isolate AI as their cause.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evidence shows broad rejection or continuing lack of confidence in Google's AI competitive and commercial position through the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence shows meaningful acceptance of Google's AI pitch among prominent Wall Street institutions, inconsistent with categorical failure.
